title: Emergent SSH physics and localization in a cavity--atom system beyond the rotating-wave approximation
authors: H. Shen, J. Cao, R. Wang, X. Z. Zhang
abstract: We investigate a cavity--atom system beyond the rotating-wave approximation and recast its dynamics as an effective tight-binding problem in the excitation-number basis. The same experimentally relevant light--matter platform exhibits two distinct regimes controlled by the photon number. In the large-photon-number regime, the hopping amplitudes become nearly uniform and the effective lattice reduces to a dimerized SSH-type chain subject to a linear energy gradient. The spectrum then organizes into one or two Wannier--Stark ladders, giving rise to controllable Bloch and Bloch--Zener oscillations and quantitatively explaining the observed revival patterns. In the small-photon-number regime, the intrinsic $\sqrt{\bar n+(\cdots)}$ dependence produces a pronounced hopping deformation, namely dimerized couplings that increase along the excitation-number lattice. This deformation reshapes the density of states, enhances collective localization, and generates an energy-resolved spatial bias of the eigenstates. The corresponding real-time dynamics displays direction-dependent anomalous diffusion together with Bloch-like revivals and beat phenomena in selected parameter windows. Our results show that the same cavity--atom platform can realize both emergent ladder spectra and hopping-induced localization in excitation-number space.
summary: This paper analyzes a cavity-atom system by mapping its dynamics onto an effective 1D lattice model. It shows that the system exhibits two distinct regimes: a large-photon-number regime yielding SSH-type physics with controllable Bloch oscillations, and a small-photon-number regime inducing strong hopping deformation and localization. This highlights the tunability of quantum transport in cavity QED platforms.
main_problem: The paper investigates emergent SSH physics and localization in a cavity-atom system by analyzing its dynamics beyond the rotating-wave approximation.
main_result: The system can realize both emergent ladder spectra (in the large-photon-number regime) and hopping-induced localization (in the small-photon-number regime) using the same physical platform.
method: The dynamics are recast into an effective tight-binding problem in the excitation-number basis, analyzed using perturbation theory and by examining different parameter regimes.
model_or_system: The physical system is a superconducting microwave resonator coupled to an effective two-level artificial atom (Cavity-QED platform). The dynamics are modeled by a generalized quantum Rabi Hamiltonian projected onto effective 1D lattice Hamiltonians.
key_observables: Bloch and Bloch-Zener oscillations, anomalous diffusion, density of states reshaping, and return probability $R(t)$.
important_parameters: Photon number ($ ar{n}$), Stark frequency ($\omega$), and coupling strengths ($\lambda_1, \lambda_2, \Omega$).
main_assumptions: The analysis involves projecting the dynamics onto invariant subspaces ($\mathbb{Z}_2$ parity) and analyzing distinct limits, such as the large-photon-number limit ($ ar{n} \gg 2N$).

paper_structure: The paper progresses from deriving the effective Hamiltonian by projecting the full Rabi model, analyzing the large-$ ar{n}$ limit to show SSH-type behavior and Bloch oscillations, and finally examining the small-$ ar{n}$ limit to reveal hopping-induced localization and anomalous diffusion.
why_interesting: This work provides a detailed theoretical framework for engineering synthetic quantum transport landscapes using cavity QED, demonstrating how non-RWA terms lead to rich physics like SSH models and localization.

Figure 4(b) shows that MIPR increases from near zero in the uniform limit to a ﬁnite value once hopping defor- mation is present. This indicates that localization is en- hanced for a broad portion of the spectrum, rather than being a feature of isolated states. A ﬁnite MIPR indi- cates that a substantial fraction of the spectrum consists of non-extended states, in agreement with the turning- point interpretation.
